A firm with a female-name contact advantage ranks low on the signed gap yet high in absolute gap size.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Both target-specific cards.** Searches each expected-rank order using at most 4 grades at τ .20; each report is optimal within this order.
- **Every changed pair.** The “Complete list of changed unordered pairs” shows every relation that appears, disappears, or reverses.
- **All firm summaries.** “All firms in released ID order” lists central intervals, expected ranks, and grades across all 97 firms.

<details>
<summary>Target-specific probabilities and precision notes</summary>

The two reports use different posterior pair probabilities. To compute probabilities for absolute gaps, the transformation applies throughout the posterior distribution (`pr_case_krw` supplies separate signed and folded cells); signed means or signed direction probabilities alone cannot recover the absolute report. A shared grade leaves the direction between two firms unstated.

Both precision plots use the original sampling SE of the signed estimate as a precision covariate. Firms in the middle grade can still differ in their contact gaps.

</details>

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The app checks its signed grade assignments against KRW's published gender card.
